title: The app shell
summary: Four tabs, a back button that goes up to where each page was opened from, an address for every page, and a layout that follows the window.
description: One interface for a phone, a tablet and a computer, built from a small design system.

stories.as: a learner using a phone and a computer
stories.want: the same app laid out for each screen

stories.as: a learner moving around the app
stories.want: back to take me to where I came from, and every page to keep its place
stories.soThat: I always know where back goes, on Android and everywhere else

requirements.text: The app's tabs are `nav.tabs`.
Exercises is the home screen: today's lessons on top, then the courses.

Back — Android's button, a page's ← and a summary's Done alike — goes up: it closes a sheet first, then goes to the page the open page was opened from, then from another tab to Exercises, and leaves the app only from Exercises.

history.text: Android's back button closes a sheet first, then the page, then goes from another tab to Exercises, and leaves the app only from Exercises.
history.reason: Back went to different places depending on how a page was reached and which control was used; one rule now holds for every way back.

requirements.text: Below `layout.rail-from` of window width the tabs are at the bottom; from `layout.rail-from` they form a rail at the left edge.
From `layout.split-from` a course's or a lesson's page is laid out in two columns, and Settings shows its menu beside the open page.
Search lists every word and sentence in the app, met or not, filterable by course and searchable in Polish or English.
On Android the page lays out above the keyboard, and the tab bar is hidden while typing.
Light and dark themes are both supported; the theme is a setting of the device.
The design system's buttons are `control.md` high by default and `control.sm` in their small size.
Destructive actions use the design system's confirm button, which asks before acting.
The design system has an empty state for lists, which says what would be there and can offer the action that fills it.
The build fails when a screen breaks the design system's mechanical rules.
The brand colour is `color.brand`, the background `color.bg` and body text `color.text`, each with its own value in the dark theme.
A right answer is shown in `color.ok` and a wrong one in `color.bad`.
All text is set in `font.family`.

Every page has an address: its tab, then each page it was opened through, things named by their id; opening an address shows that page with the same way back, and a sheet belongs to the page under it.
A course, lesson, song or tutor conversation opened from another page opens in the tab that page is in, above it, and back returns to that page.
Going back to a page shows it as it was left: the same section, scrolled where it was.
Reopened within `nav.resume-within` of leaving it, the app shows the page that was open; a drill, a conversation, a summary or the player is not reopened, the page under it is.
Tapping a notification opens what it is about: a tutor reply its conversation, a reminder Exercises, a download its course, playback the player.
Leaving a drill or a conversation after answering asks first, with `nav.leave-drill` or `nav.leave-conversation`; back while it is being graded does nothing.
Tapping a tab shows it where it was last left; tapping the tab already shown goes to its top.
On a computer, Cmd+[ and the mouse's back button go back.
A page's address is the same at every window width; picking another item in a two-column list replaces the one open, so back leaves the list in one step.
Opening a page already among those the open page was opened through goes back to it, and an address holds at most `nav.max-depth` pages.
When what a page shows is deleted, on this device or another, the page gives way to the nearest page above it that still exists.
